findings.title: Spawned workers bypass the restart kill guard
findings.description:
Workers are created using `multiprocessing.get_context("spawn").Process`, which produces `multiprocessing.context.SpawnProcess` instances. These are not instances of the separate `multiprocessing.Process` class, so the new `isinstance` guard skips `kill()` in production.

When a worker hangs, its replacement starts while the old worker remains alive. If the old worker resumes, both can flush the same shards, risking duplicate output and conflicting Redis cleanup. Check against `multiprocessing.process.BaseProcess` or explicitly distinguish threads, and ensure the old worker exits before replacing it. Add coverage using a spawned worker rather than only the thread-based test path.

findings.title: An expired join deadline skips remaining worker cleanup
findings.description:
Once the deadline expires, `break` skips cleanup for every remaining worker. This also happens for all workers if `next_step.join(timeout)` consumes the available time. Setting `stopped` is insufficient for workers blocked in Redis or Kafka operations, so old workers can survive a rebalance and overlap with the next strategy's workers.

Apply the deadline only to graceful waiting; still terminate and reap every remaining process afterward. The process-type check must also recognize `SpawnProcess`. Test shutdown with multiple workers, including a blocked worker and an already-expired deadline.

findings.title: Memory checks query the entire Redis cluster once per worker
findings.description:
Each buffer's `get_memory_info()` calls `iter_cluster_memory_usage(self.client)`, which retrieves memory information for the entire Redis cluster, not only the buffer's assigned shards. Consequently, when memory backpressure is enabled, every submission repeats the same cluster-wide query once per flusher worker.

The duplicated totals provide no additional coverage and multiply synchronous Redis work as parallelism increases. Query cluster memory once per submission using a single buffer or shared client.

findings.title: The added test delay is patched into a no-op
findings.description:
The test patches `time.sleep` to `lambda _: None`, so the newly added `time.sleep(0.1)` does not give the flusher time to process the changed drift. `step.join()` immediately sets the stop flag, leaving the assertion dependent on whether the background thread happened to flush beforehand.

Replace the delay with deterministic synchronization—for example, wait with a bounded timeout on an event signaled by the output callback—before shutting down the strategy.
